Topics · One God, one message

Why call it Islam if earlier prophets came first?

The Quran says the name is older than the Quran: on the lips of Noah, Abraham, Jacob, Moses and the disciples.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَجَـٰهِدُوا۟ فِى ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦ ۚ هُوَ ٱجْتَبَىٰكُمْ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ ۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ مِن قَبْلُ وَفِى هَـٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ ۚ فَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوْلَىٰكُمْ ۖ فَنِعْمَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَنِعْمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And strive for Allāh with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. He [i.e., Allāh] named you "Muslims" before [in former scriptures] and in this [revelation] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakāh and hold fast to Allāh. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:78

Translation

For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.

Original · Ancient Greek

αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν, καὶ αἱ ἐντολαὶ αὐτοῦ βαρεῖαι οὐκ εἰσίν,

1 John · 5:3

World English Bible

The question is fair: how can people before the seventh century carry a name that appeared then? The Quran answers against what you may expect: the name did not begin with it. The verse says God named you Muslims before, and in this. So the claim is that the naming came before this book. If so, the question turns over: the later people did not hand their name to the earlier; they joined what the earlier already were. The verse ties this openly to the way of Abraham.

A question for you

If the name is older than the Quran, who owns it?

If you sayNo one owns it
ThenThat changes what it means to carry it, for a Muslim before anyone else.
If you sayMuslims today
ThenThey carry it today, on the Quran's account. You may ask whether carrying is the same as owning.
If you sayI do not accept that it is older
ThenThat is your right; the claim rests on the Quran alone. The next part shows its internal witnesses, for you to weigh.

Part 2 of 3

﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥٓ أَسْلِمْ ۖ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ١٣١ وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ يَـٰبَنِىَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ١٣٢ أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ ٱلْمَوْتُ إِذْ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعْدِى قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ إِلَـٰهَكَ وَإِلَـٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسْمَـٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَـٰقَ إِلَـٰهًا وَٰحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَ١٣٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted [in Islām][45] to the Lord of the worlds." And Abraham instructed his sons [to do the same] and [so did] Jacob, [saying], "O my sons, indeed Allāh has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims." Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God.[46] And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."

Translator's notes

[45] The meaning of the word "Islām" is "submission to the will of Allāh." This is the way of life ordained by Allāh and taught by all of the prophets from Adam to Muḥammad (ﷺ). A Muslim is one who submits himself to Allāh.

[46] Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) alone.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:131-133

Translation

For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that Yahweh may bring on Abraham that which he has spoken of him.”

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֣י יְדַעְתִּ֗יו לְמַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֶת־בָּנָ֤יו וְאֶת־בֵּיתוֹ֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְשָֽׁמְרוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת צְדָקָ֖ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט לְמַ֗עַן הָבִ֤יא יְהוָה֙ עַל־אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֖ר עָלָֽיו׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 18:19

World English Bible

Take the word at the time it is placed. Abraham was told: surrender, and he said: I surrender to the Lord of the worlds. He charged his sons with it, and so did Jacob as he lay dying, asking his sons: what will you serve after me? They answered with one God and with surrender. The scene matters: a dying man leaving his children something that cannot be held in the hand, and those children are the ones a whole people is later named after.

A question for you

If someone you love asked you at the last: what will you serve after me? what would you honestly say?

Part 3 of 3

﴿مَا كَانَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلَا نَصْرَانِيًّا وَلَـٰكِن كَانَ حَنِيفًا مُّسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

﴿فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ قَالَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But when Jesus felt [persistence in] disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allāh?" The disciples said, "We are supporters for Allāh. We have believed in Allāh and testify that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].

Quran · Aal Imran 3:52

If this claim holds, something follows that is hard for every side to say, Muslims included: the name is enough for no one. The first verse says Abraham was neither Jew nor Christian but upright and surrendered, so he stood before the labels. The second places the word on the lips of the disciples of Jesus. A meaning wide enough for these cannot become a party's flag. So the question for a Muslim today: do you carry the name, or does the name carry you?

A question for you

What does this do to the person who carries the name?

If you sayIt widens who belongs
ThenYes, backward in time. The Quran keeps the condition of faith in every messenger who has reached you, so widening does not mean levelling.
If you sayIt asks more of them
ThenThat is what the verse does with anyone resting on a name, a Muslim included.
If you sayI find it hard to accept
ThenUnderstood: to hear your prophets called by a word you know from another community is heavy. That deserves an honest look.
